newsitem.title: USA: Intel stock surges after revenue forecast.
newsitem.headline: Intel stock surges after revenue forecast.

text.p: Intel Corp.'s stock sizzled Tuesday, a day after the world's No. 1 computer chip maker said its third-quarter earnings would be better than previously predicted.

Intel stock climbed to a 52-week high, hitting $94.625 in late morning trading on Nasdaq, a rise of $6 or nearly 7 percent, before slipping to $93.75 in the early afternoon. It was the most actively traded stock, with volume of more than 13 million shares.

Many Wall Street analysts raised their earnings forecasts and ratings for Intel following the chip maker's announcement late Monday. Several said the good news from Intel -- which holds a near-monopoly on the market for personal computer microprocessors -- was also good news for other chip makers and the rest of the PC industry.
"This suggests the PC industry is quite healthy," said Charles Boucher of UBS securities.

Other semiconductor stocks rose on Intel's coattails. S3 Inc., which supplies graphics accelerator chips for PCs, rose $1.125 to $17.125; integrated circuit maker Atmel Corp. jumped $1.625 to $25.75; and Applied Materials, which makes wafer fabrication systems for the semiconductor industry, gained $1.375 to $27.125, all on Nasdaq.

All three stocks joined Intel on the top 10 list of most actively traded stocks. The Phliadelphia Stock Exchange's Semiconductor Index rose 6.77 points to 179.85 and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite index climbed 5.15 points to 1,199.11.

"This could even filter down to the equipment suppliers," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. Intel makes the microprocessors that are the heart of 80 percent of the personal computers in the world.
When Intel reported its second-quarter earnings in July, it predicted the next quarter's revenues would not increase.

But late Monday, after the market closed, the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company said it expected third-quarter revenues would be 5 percent higher than the second quarter's $4.62 billion. Intel plans to report third-quarter results Oct. 14.

In last year's third quarter, the company made a profit of $931 million, or $1.05 per share, on sales of $4.17 billion. The consensus estimate for this year's third quarter is $1.14 per share, according to the First Call service, which tracks analyst forecasts.

Intel also said Monday that its gross margins -- the difference between the sales price for its products and the costs of raw materials and manufacturing -- would exceed its model of 50 percent, plus or minus a couple of points. Intel's gross margin in the second quarter was 53 percent.
Intel said business levels were hard to predict because the semiconductor industry is in an environment where PC manufacturers order chips just before they need them on assembly lines.
Intel's stock soared in after-hours trading Monday and continued its climb after the market opened Tuesday.
